item.title: World-renowned musician and Shannonside presenter conferred with trad music award
item.description: A local world-renowned musician and Shannonside Northern Sound presenter has been conferred with an award in honour of his contribution to Irish trad music. The Heathery Breeze presenter Paddy Ryan received the Dr John Stafford award at the Elphin Community Centre last night. The award is conferred to those who provide outstanding service to Irish traditional music in Roscommon. The famous fiddle player and teacher says he wasn't expecting the award: Advertisement

item.title: Over €6 million spent on advisers for local TD
item.description: It's been revealed local TD Peter Burke is the biggest spender on spin. This comprises money paid to 31 members of staff within his department's communications unit, as well as 64 employees in ten agencies under his control, including the IDA, Enterprise Ireland, Fáilte Ireland and Tourism Ireland. item.title: Castlecoote native says plans underway to get TEDx event back to Athlone next year
item.description: A Castlecoote native played a central role in bringing the first-ever TEDx event to Athlone last week. MaryJo Neilan, marketing coordinator with TUS Athlone, was co-organiser of the landmark event at the Dean Crowe Theatre. Speakers on the night included Midlands-North-West MEP Ciaran Mullooly, radio presenter Dave Duke, and vascular surgeon Dr Niamh Hynes. MaryJo says there are already plans to get the event back to Athlone next year: Advertisement

item.title: New off-street parking must be made available before redesign plans for Ballymahon - local councillor
item.description: A local councillor says new off-street parking must be made available before any parking spaces is removed in Ballymahon. A Town Centre First Information event took place last week in Ballymahon Library. Proposed redesign plans for Garvey's Yard, Annaly Car Park and Weaver's Hall entrance were the main focus at event. Fine Gael Cllr Paul Ross addressed concerns that some parking in the town may be lost as a result of new plans: Advertisement

item.title: Antrim land victory over Leitrim
item.description: Antrim produced a powerful second-half display to secure a convincing 2-19 to 1-13 victory over Leitrim in Carrick-on-Shannon. With a strong wind at their backs in the opening period. The visitors made full use of the conditions to build a commanding half-time lead before finishing strongly to seal a nine-point win. Leitrim who opened the scoring in Páirc Seán, Mark Diffley splitting the posts with a superb two-pointer after 10 minutes. Advertisement However, Antrim eventually found their range.
